Timeline::TimelineIndexAccessor::slice_time¶

Back to Timeline Index Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

pluss::Series Timeline::TimelineIndexAccessor::slice_time(std::string_view start_iso, std::string_view end_iso) const

What It Does¶

Returns the matching positional indices for an inclusive slice specified with ISO-like text bounds.

This is the convenience overload of slice. It is usually the surface you want when the bounds already exist as timestamp strings in config, user input, or glue code.

The temporal semantics stay the same as slice(). The only difference is that string parsing happens inside the call instead of before it.

Parameters¶

start_iso

Inclusive lower bound written as an ISO-like timestamp string.

Explicit timezone information is safer when correctness matters.

end_iso

Inclusive upper bound written as an ISO-like timestamp string.

Returns¶

pluss::Series A 1D integer Series of matching positions.

Examples¶

Example 1. Slice directly from ISO-like text bounds.

auto rows = idx.slice_time(
    "2024-11-01T00:15:00Z",
    "2024-11-01T01:00:00Z");
std::cout << pluss::series::print(rows) << "\n";

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 2, 3]

Example 2. Use config-provided bounds without first constructing scalar Timeline objects by hand.

std::string from_cfg = "2024-11-01T00:15:00Z";
std::string to_cfg = "2024-11-01T01:00:00Z";

auto rows = idx.slice_time(from_cfg, to_cfg);
std::cout << pluss::series::print(rows) << "\n";

This is the most natural form when the bounds already live in metadata, configuration, or user-facing text input.

Notes¶

  • slice_time() is functionally the same idea as slice; it just moves scalar parsing inside the call.

  • Reach for slice() instead when the bounds are already Timeline scalars in the surrounding code.

  • Explicit timezone suffixes such as Z or -07:00 are safer than ambiguous local strings when correctness matters.

See Also¶

  • Timeline::TimelineIndexAccessor::slice: same semantics, but scalar Timeline bounds.

  • Timeline::TimelineIndexAccessor::asof: nearest previous timestamp position instead of a full range.
